- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1), model underestimates upward momentum → add 2–4% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile → adjust downward by 1–3% for short-term forecasts.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model lags in recognizing trend reversal → delay forecast rise by 1–2 days or add 1–2% buffer.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean reversion → reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment shows persistent negative trend.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (avg > 0.1) and price is rising, model tends to overforecast → cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day high.
